source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade and Downgrade BMC firmware by Web when system is booted
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade BMC firmware through web UI.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: browser/automation to drive the BMC web-UI flash page + BMC image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- BMC upgrade/downgrade via the BMC web UI: the agent first places the exact user-provided BMC image where the web-UIs upload control expects it, then drives the BMC flash page (upload image, start update, wait for completion) with the SUT must be booted and the BMC web-UI reachable; after completion verify the BMC version. Interactive web-UI upload is not a single sshpass one-liner; walk the UI steps after the image is in place.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return screenshots + the flash-completion status and the BMC version shown before/after so the user confirms a successful flash and a clean single reset.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: BMC firmware flash via web UI is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image and do not interrupt mid-flash.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes web flashing before the reset/sequence contract is defined.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; identifies the unresolved reset semantics and recovery requirements.

original_test_intent: Validate approved BMC firmware upgrade and downgrade via the live BMC WebUI while the host is booted, including exact version transitions and a precisely defined single-reset behavior.
original_method: As written, a human uses the WebUI for both directions and the system must succeed 'after BMC reset only one time'; execution is unsafe until the owner defines the ordered runs, reset initiator/count/timing and per-direction expected state.
manual_activity: If unblocked, WebUI selection/upload/confirmation and observation are manual core actions; the agent may prepare images and collect independent read-only evidence.
required_inputs: Definition of reset initiator, allowed count, timing and per-direction result
Verified image hashes/signatures and platform compatibility
WebUI SOP, configuration-preservation policy and rollback/recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not upload or start a firmware write while the reset and sequence semantics remain unresolved.
Never retry, run both directions or add a reset without a fixed approved plan.
Require stable power, a maintenance window and independent recovery path.
Preserve all raw failures and stop on reachability/host-state uncertainty.
agent_execution_scope: Perform only read-only baseline, image verification and evidence-plan preparation while blocked.
After correction, support independent version/health/log collection but do not operate or claim completion of the WebUI core.
engineer_actions: Define the version/order/reset contract and approve compatible images/recovery.
If unblocked, execute the WebUI operation and issue separate upgrade/downgrade verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Premature: it authorizes upload/start despite undefined reset count, version sequence and recovery; it is not executable safely.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: None while blocked; after correction use the vendor WebUI manually and independent read-only IPMI/Redfish version/health checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The WebUI, booted-host, upgrade/downgrade and 5/15-minute facts remain; no target/reset meaning is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define each direction as an approved transition with immutable image identity, one explicit activation/reset event, configuration-preservation expectations and independent post-reset verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until the exact BMC model/build and image pair are approved.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/host/browser/WebUI, image and verification-interface versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor BMC update/recovery documentation and release-owner transition matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes reset semantics, sequence, recovery and independent verification explicit.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents an arbitrary reset or partial browser success from satisfying both upgrade and downgrade.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware writes can strand management; browser status alone is not proof of installed/healthy firmware.

project_override_considerations: A project may define versions and reset behavior, but the approved override must state exactly which transition(s) were completed and cannot claim the unspecified library matrix.
expected_evidence: If unblocked: complete WebUI transcript and reset timeline

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source is not internally contradictory, but the phrase 'after BMC reset only one time' leaves an essential destructive-operation semantic undefined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Without the reset initiator/count/timing and ordered upgrade/downgrade contract, the necessary firmware operation cannot be executed or judged safely; this exceeds an ordinary missing project parameter.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its BLOCKED decision and retains the required clarification/recovery gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Uses NEED_ENGINEER_DECISION rather than inventing a global reset policy or treating missing images alone as the block.

review_improvement: Prevents a high-risk firmware write from proceeding under an acceptance phrase that cannot determine whether an automatic reset, manual reset or second transition is allowed.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware transition safety and acceptance depend on a deterministic state machine; 'only one reset' is not executable until its trigger and relationship to two version directions are defined.
